$comment: Language-neutral golden vectors for the safety-critical generic gates in @quran-ai/contracts.
The basis-optional canShowLearnerFacingAiOutput cases here cover AgentRun compatibility.
Acoustic Tajweed findings use fixtures/learner-feedback-gate.json, which Rust, Node, Dart,
and the TypeScript contract execute directly. Do not add acoustic cases to this generic corpus.
The remaining groups pin retention, external ASR, release evaluation, hashing, and recited marks.

canShowLearnerFacingAiOutput.$comment: Generic AgentRun allowlist: teacher-reviewed/scholar-approved, finite confidence in [0.82,1], and at least one source. Explicit text-rule output is refused. Acoustic findings use learner-feedback-gate.json.

cases.name: approved: scholar-approved also clears the gate
blocked: a teacher REJECTED this finding
cases.$comment: The outcome of TeacherDecision::Rejected (handlers/review.rs sets review_status to 'blocked'). It was absent from this corpus until a test cross-referenced the tajweed_findings CHECK constraint and found the vocabulary had six values while the table exercised five -- so every implementation of the gate was verified without ever being shown the single most consequential result of the review workflow: a human looking at a judgement about a child's recitation and saying no. Confidence and sources are deliberately GENEROUS here; neither may rescue a rejection.

cases.name: FAILS CLOSED: unrecognized reviewStatus must block, never pass
cases.$comment: THE most important case in this corpus. reviewStatus arrives from an HTTP JSON body with no server-side schema enforcement, so a typo or a future upstream status lands here as an unknown string. An allowlist returns false; a denylist of known-bad statuses would return TRUE and leak unreviewed output to a learner. A port using a language enum (Dart, Rust) may reject or coerce this value instead of evaluating it -- that port is wrong even if its own tests pass.

cases.name: blocked: instructional text rule is not learner-performance feedback

mustDiscardAudio.$comment: Retention gate: is this recording one we are OBLIGED to destroy? An ALLOWLIST of the two modes that permit keeping audio, not a denylist containing 'discard'. The difference is the out-of-vocabulary case: a denylist answers 'no, you may keep it' for a retention value nobody recognises, which retains a child's recording under a policy no one can state. services/ml-inference's retention sweep has always classified anything it does not recognise as discard-TTL; this function used to disagree with it, and no case here had ever shown either of them an unknown value.

cases.name: FAILS CLOSED: an unrecognised retention mode must be destroyed
cases.$comment: The case neither implementation had ever been shown. `audio_retention` reaches this from a consent record and from a ticket claim carried as an unvalidated string (shared-ticket/src/lib.rs says so explicitly, on the grounds that an unknown value can only SHORTEN retention -- which is only true if every consumer treats unknown as discard). A denylist of 'discard' answers false here: keep a recording under a policy nobody can state.

cases.name: FAILS CLOSED: an empty retention mode must be destroyed

canUseExternalAsr.$comment: AND gate: BOTH externalAsrProcessing AND guardianApproved must be true. All three false-combinations are pinned so a port cannot implement OR by mistake.

cases.name: both false: blocked (pins the AND, not an OR)

modelEvalPassesReleaseGate.$comment: Legacy aggregate vectors. None carries a cryptographically verified row-level evidence authority, so every case MUST fail closed even when its arithmetic looks passing. Release-authority success and tamper cases live in tests/release/model-evidence.test.mjs.

cases.name: aggregate thresholds alone are not release authority
any unsourced learner output is disqualifying
passed flag false overrides all metrics

sha256Hex.$comment: Byte-level cross-language anchor. UTF-8 is the ONLY correct byte source: Dart's String.codeUnits is UTF-16 and Java/Kotlin's default charset is platform-dependent -- both produce a different digest for the Arabic vector below while agreeing with TS on the ASCII ones. That is why an Arabic case is mandatory here, not optional.

cases.name: arabic with diacritics (UTF-8, NOT UTF-16)
cases.$note: A UTF-16 byte source yields 4595330cb3470c17227f05845841b9b7c670a71870d7c53813e5a806ebc79881 for this same string -- verified, not assumed. That is why an Arabic vector is mandatory: the two ASCII cases above pass under BOTH encodings, so they cannot catch a Dart port using String.codeUnits.

cases.name: supplementary-plane (surrogate pair) — catches what the Arabic case does NOT
cases.$comment: U+1EE00 + U+1EE01: 2 code points, 4 UTF-16 code units. The Arabic vector already catches a naive UTF-16 byte source, but NOT an implementation that iterates by code UNIT and splits a surrogate pair — that produces two lone surrogates, which encode to U+FFFD in UTF-8 and give a different digest. Dart's String.runes and Swift's Character are correct here; String.codeUnits and a JS for-loop over .length are not.

cases.name: NFC-unstable canonical text — normalizing CHANGES the digest
cases.$comment: inputCodepoints, NOT a literal: writing combining marks as characters is how PR #258 shipped a regex that deleted every Arabic letter, and while adding THIS vector the literal was silently reordered in transit and produced the normalized digest. Codepoints cannot be reordered by a tool that touches the file. U+0628 U+0651 U+064E (beh, shadda, fatha) reorders under NFC to U+0628 U+064E U+0651 — the dominant transform among the 5,771 of 6,236 ayahs that are NFC-unstable (MIG4). A client that normalizes gets `wrongIfNormalized` and invalidates verifyCanonicalWord across 89 of 114 surahs.

isNonRecitedMark.$comment: T1 — mushaf annotation vs recited word. inputCodepoints (not literal characters) because these marks are INVISIBLE in an editor and in a diff: a literal-character class in forced_align.py merged two ranges, deleted every Arabic letter, and passed review (PR #258). AGENTS.md makes escapes a hard boundary. A Dart/Node port builds the string from the codepoints and must agree.

cases.name: U+06DE start of rub el hizb
real word bismi — must stay scored
word CARRYING a mark is still a word (the dangerous loose rule would drop it)
whitespace only cannot be a mark
word-internal combining mark U+06EC is not standalone annotation
